newsitem.title: INDIA: Cricket-India make four changes in squad.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-India make four changes in squad.

text.p: India on Tuesday made four changes in their squad for a triangular limited-overs series and altered travel plans to give their beleaguered cricketers a rest before a tour of the West Indies.

Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) Secretary Jagmohan Dalmiya said opener Woorkeri Raman, middle-order batsman Pankaj Dharmani, left-arm spinner Venkatapathy Raju and medium-pacer David Johnson had been omitted from the one-day squad.

They will return to India after the third and final test against South Africa which begins in Johannesburg on Wednesday. Zimbabwe will join India and South Africa for the triangular series which runs from January 23 to February 13.

The selectors, who had a tele-conference with Indian captain Sachin Tendulkar and coach Madan Lal, named batsman Ajay Jadeja, all-rounders Robin Singh and Sunil Joshi and medium-pacer Salil Ankola as the replacements.
India, struggling against South Africa's pace attack on bouncy wickets, have suffered big defeats in the first two tests, provoking widespread protests at home over the squad selection.
"The replacements are not on the basis of the performance of these four players but it was decided that these replacements will help the side perform better in one-dayers," Dalmiya told reporters.
Dalmiya also announced a change in the tour schedule. The Indian team will return home after the two-match one-day series in Zimbabwe and go to the West Indies after a week's break.
Originally the squad was to have gone from South Africa to Zimbabwe and then to the West Indies, where they will play five tests and five one-day internationals.
